excerpts.text: - 2026-05-15 01:20 +0800: Implemented and tested SegLLM-style MR-LISA++ v1 input-stream `[REF]` conditioning. Key code changes: `mr_ref_seg_dataset.py` now creates true two-round conversations and CLIP crops for reference masks; `dataset.py` collates `ref_images_clip`; `llava_llama.py` injects reference embeddings at `[REF]` positions before LLM forward; `LISA.py` adds ref crop+bbox input projection and `[REF]` reconstruction loss; `train_ds.py`, merge, and counterfactual eval support `[REF]`. Important bug fixes from pilots: fixed `ref_token_idx` fallback because `convert_tokens_to_ids("[REF]")` returned `-1`; fixed `LISAForCausalLM.__init__` to read token ids from config overrides; prevented unconditional `initialize_lisa_modules()` from wiping loaded LISA weights; changed ref input to residual injection and added optional `RESET_REF_INPUT_PROJECTION=1`. Built counterfactual grouped training data at `/home/wjq/cmllm/outputs/mr_data/helmet_miner_pseudopair_v1/final_accepted_v1/counterfactual_train_v1`: combined train 13,455 rows = 9,724 regular + 3,731 grouped counterfactual; holdout regular 2,494; holdout counterfactual 921. Training/testing sequence: pilot200 without counterfactual reached ordinary val Round1/2 IoU 0.559/0.543 but RCS 0; cf_pilot300 before token-id fix reached ordinary holdout 0.653/0.681 but RCS 0; after token-id and constructor fixes, `refactive_cf_pilot500` trained with real `[REF]` gradients and nonzero RefMaskLoss, merged at `/home/wjq/cmllm/outputs/lisa_finetune/cmllm_lisa_plus_mr_ref_v1_refactive_cf_pilot500_20260515_0058/merged_hf`. Its ordinary holdout 100-sample test: Round1 miner mean IoU 0.7063, Round2 helmet mean IoU 0.6760, IoU>0.5 = 0.83/0.77. Counterfactual holdout 300: mean IoU correct 0.4110, wrong 0.4082, mean RCS 0.00279, median RCS 0.00036, pair success 0.50. Source/counterfactual 300 was similarly weak (mean RCS 0.00217). Conclusion: v1 now has a working internal `[REF]` path and preserves/improves ordinary MR segmentation, but REF target-switching remains weak; next revision should add stronger Round2/counterfactual weighting or an explicit differentiable ranking loss `IoU(correct REF target) > IoU(wrong REF target)` instead of relying on mask BCE/Dice alone.

- 2026-05-15 12:00 +0800: Implemented and tested MR-LISA++ v2A SegLLM-focus revision after re-reading SegLLM's mask encoding: `[REF]` input now supports strong/gated injection, `LISA.py` can feed a `[REF]` prompt context together with `[SEG]` into the SAM prompt encoder, ref reconstruction default weight is 1.0, and training/merge scripts expose `ref_prompt_mode`, `ref_injection_mode`, `ref_input_scale`, `ref_context_init_scale`, `ref_prompt_max_norm`, and `sam_prompt_embed_clamp`. Added scripts `run_lisa_finetune_mr_ref_v2_segllm_focus.sh` and `run_eval_mr_ref_counterfactual_v2_segllm_focus.sh`. The most aggressive `replace + concat` variant produced NaNs on some samples; the stable variant uses `gated_add`, `ref_input_scale=0.5`, `ref_prompt_mode=add`, `ref_context_init_scale=0.2`, plus prompt/mask `nan_to_num` guards. A 50-step smoke on H100 GPU1 completed with 0 NaNs. The 500-step pilot completed and merged successfully at `/home/wjq/cmllm/outputs/lisa_finetune/cmllm_lisa_plus_mr_ref_v2_segllm_focus_nanguard_pilot500_20260515_114452/merged_hf`, trained on 13,455 combined regular+counterfactual rows with 0 NaNs. Counterfactual holdout evaluation: 300-sample mean IoU correct 0.4067, wrong 0.3980, mean RCS 0.00876, median RCS 0.0, pair success 0.4883; full 921-sample holdout mean IoU correct 0.3552, wrong 0.3454, mean RCS 0.00973, median RCS 0.0, pair success 0.4739, counterfactual success 0.0163. Interpretation: explicit SegLLM-style reference/focus modifications create a weak positive `[REF]` sensitivity signal compared with v1 (RCS about 0.0028 on 300 samples), but target switching remains unstable; next step should be a real counterfactual/ranking loss or stronger paired batch construction, not just stronger ref injection.

- 2026-05-15 12:35 +0800: Implemented MR-LISA++ v2B counterfactual ranking loss. `model/LISA.py` now computes a differentiable soft-IoU matrix for grouped counterfactual samples and adds `max(0, margin + IoU(pred_i, wrong_helmet) - IoU(pred_i, correct_helmet))`, only for same-image grouped `[miner, helmet] * N` batches. `train_ds.py` logs `RankLoss`, merge preserves `counterfactual_rank_*` config, and `run_lisa_finetune_mr_ref_v2b_rank.sh` starts from the stable v2A merged model with `counterfactual_rank_loss_weight=0.5`, `counterfactual_rank_margin=0.05`. A 50-step smoke completed on H100 GPU1 with 15/50 nonzero RankLoss steps, max RankLoss 0.2404, and no training NaNs. A 500-step pilot completed and merged at `/home/wjq/cmllm/outputs/lisa_finetune/cmllm_lisa_plus_mr_ref_v2b_rank_pilot500_20260515_1218/merged_hf`; train count 13,455, no eval during training. Counterfactual holdout evaluation improved substantially over v2A: 300-sample mean IoU correct 0.4292, wrong 0.3663, mean RCS 0.06295, median RCS 0.05684, pair success 0.5550, counterfactual success 0.1100; full 921-sample holdout mean IoU correct 0.4095, wrong 0.3271, mean RCS 0.08234, median RCS 0.07694, pair success 0.5630, counterfactual success 0.1336. Interpretation: v2B confirms true counterfactual/ranking supervision is the first change that clearly improves `[REF]` target switching; the model still is not fully stable, but it now has measurable REF-dependent behavior rather than near-zero RCS.

- 2026-05-15 14:35 +0800: Continued v2B ranking training for a full 13,455-step pseudo-epoch from the v2B-500 merged model, testing two conservative LR=1e-5 branches in parallel: A `counterfactual_rank_loss_weight=0.5` on GPU1 and B `counterfactual_rank_loss_weight=1.0` on GPU2. Both finished `global_step13455`, merged successfully, and had no training NaNs/errors. A merged model: `/home/wjq/cmllm/outputs/lisa_finetune/cmllm_lisa_plus_mr_ref_v2b_rank_long1ep_w05_lr1e5_20260515/merged_hf`; B merged model: `/home/wjq/cmllm/outputs/lisa_finetune/cmllm_lisa_plus_mr_ref_v2b_rank_long1ep_w10_lr1e5_20260515/merged_hf`. Full 921 counterfactual holdout: A mean IoU correct 0.8934, wrong 0.0117, mean RCS 0.8817, median RCS 0.9577, pair success 0.9723, counterfactual success 0.9446; B mean IoU correct 0.8965, wrong 0.0123, mean RCS 0.8842, median RCS 0.9580, pair success 0.9745, counterfactual success 0.9490. Full 2,494 regular holdout eval also remained healthy: A giou/ciou 0.7055/0.5151, B 0.7088/0.5220. Interpretation: training duration was a major factor; the one-pseudo-epoch ranking continuation converts the previously weak REF sensitivity into strong same-query REF target switching. The B branch is the current best candidate by both counterfactual and regular holdout metrics.

- 2026-05-15 15:30 +0800: Attempted a second continuation round from the current best B model to search for an even higher peak, with planned branches `rank_weight=0.5/1.0/1.5`, LR=5e-6, 13,455 steps. The first three-way launch and then a single `rank_weight=1.0` relaunch did not reach training: deepspeed launcher processes stayed in CPU startup, wrote 0-byte logs, and never occupied GPU. Afterward H100 SSH became intermittently unresponsive; `ssh H100 "echo alive"` timed out during banner exchange. No second-continuation training result exists yet. Current best remains `/home/wjq/cmllm/outputs/lisa_finetune/cmllm_lisa_plus_mr_ref_v2b_rank_long1ep_w10_lr1e5_20260515/merged_hf`. When H100 SSH recovers, first clean up any `v2b_rank_long2ep_*` tmux/session remnants, then retry only a single branch before parallelizing.

- 2026-05-16 02:00 +0800: H100 SSH recovered and the second v2B ranking continuation completed successfully. A 100-step smoke from the previous best B model passed first, then three full 13,455-step branches were trained from `/home/wjq/cmllm/outputs/lisa_finetune/cmllm_lisa_plus_mr_ref_v2b_rank_long1ep_w10_lr1e5_20260515/merged_hf` with LR=5e-6 and `rank_weight=0.5/1.0/1.5`. All three merged without training NaNs/errors: `w05` `/home/wjq/cmllm/outputs/lisa_finetune/cmllm_lisa_plus_mr_ref_v2b_rank_long2ep_w05_lr5e6_20260515/merged_hf`, `w10` `/home/wjq/cmllm/outputs/lisa_finetune/cmllm_lisa_plus_mr_ref_v2b_rank_long2ep_w10_lr5e6_20260515/merged_hf`, and `w15` `/home/wjq/cmllm/outputs/lisa_finetune/cmllm_lisa_plus_mr_ref_v2b_rank_long2ep_w15_lr5e6_20260515/merged_hf`. Full 921 counterfactual holdout: `w05` correct/wrong/RCS/medianRCS/pair/CF = 0.9118/0.0048/0.9070/0.9603/0.9864/0.9729; `w10` = 0.9077/0.0058/0.9019/0.9600/0.9826/0.9653; `w15` = 0.9087/0.0053/0.9034/0.9597/0.9832/0.9663. Full 2,494 regular holdout: `w05` giou/ciou 0.7165/0.5209, `w10` 0.7142/0.5129, `w15` 0.7193/0.5264. Interpretation: the second continuation improves beyond the first long run. If optimizing pure `[REF]` switching, `w05` is the best counterfactual model; if selecting the best balanced checkpoint, `w15` is preferred because it has the highest regular giou/ciou while still substantially improving counterfactual RCS and success over the previous best.

- 2026-05-16 12:05 +0800: Completed the requested next-stage Step 1 and Step 2. Step 1 froze the formal baseline under `/home/wjq/cmllm/outputs/mr_experiments/formal_baseline_v1`, with `BASELINE_REPORT.md`, `model_manifest.json`, a stable symlink to the primary model, and six representative visual overlays. The formal primary model remains `/home/wjq/cmllm/outputs/lisa_finetune/cmllm_lisa_plus_mr_ref_v2b_rank_long2ep_w15_lr5e6_20260515/merged_hf`; the pure REF-switch analysis checkpoint remains `w05`. Step 2 implemented SegLLM-style explicit focus/blackout input without breaking v2B reproducibility: `MultiRoundRefSegDataset` and `eval_mr_ref_counterfactual_v0.py` now support `MR_REF_IMAGE_MODE=crop|full_blackout|full_darken|full_blur`, with focus dilation/background controls, and `run_lisa_finetune_mr_ref_v3_focus.sh` wraps the v2B rank training script. A 100-step `full_blackout` smoke passed with no NaNs/errors. The 3,000-step v3-focus pilot trained from the formal `w15` model and merged at `/home/wjq/cmllm/outputs/lisa_finetune/cmllm_lisa_plus_mr_ref_v3_focus_blackout_pilot3000_20260516/merged_hf`. Quick 300-sample counterfactual looked strong (correct 0.9164, wrong 0.0016, RCS 0.9148, CF success 0.9767), but full 921 holdout was slightly below the formal `w15` baseline: correct 0.9026, wrong 0.0063, RCS 0.8963, median RCS 0.9591, pair success 0.9810, CF success 0.9620. Regular holdout was also slightly below `w15`: direct eval giou/ciou 0.7136/0.5234 versus `w15` 0.7193/0.5264. Conclusion: do not replace the formal main model with v3-focus yet. Keep v3-focus as a validated explicit focus/blackout mechanism for the next true multi-round pipeline, where focus is used as an intermediate visual operation rather than as a short continuation alone.

- 2026-05-17 17:15 +0800: Ran the fixed-scale v3 controller on a larger held-out test subset: first 300 rows of `/home/wjq/cmllm/outputs/mr_data/helmet_miner_pseudopair_v1/final_accepted_v1/counterfactual_train_v1/episodes_miner_to_helmet_regular_holdout.jsonl`, degradation `extreme`, model `w15`. Remote output: `/home/wjq/cmllm/outputs/mr_experiments/stage3_rule_controller_v3_fixed_roi/holdout300_extreme_strong_ref12_anchor15`; local copy: `D:\work\fightccfa-agin\coalminellm\cmllm_samples\stage3_rule_controller_v3_fixed_roi_holdout300_ref12_anchor15`. Compared on the same 300 rows against v2 direct-first baseline `/home/wjq/cmllm/outputs/mr_experiments/stage3_rule_controller_v2_direct_first/holdout300_extreme`: degraded direct initial mean target IoU 0.0675; v2 final mean target IoU 0.1878 with 26/300 accepted; fixed-scale v3 final mean target IoU 0.1969 with 32/300 accepted. Paired v3-v2 delta: mean +0.0092, median 0.0; 51 episodes improved, 10 worsened, 239 unchanged; v3 accepted all 26 v2-accepted cases plus 6 additional cases. Current v3 path counts: `direct_target=4`, `anchor_focus=68`, `anchor_focus_local_enhance=18`, `rollback_to_direct=45`, `direct_then_anchor_failed=165`; local segmentation attempts 441, local improvements 79, local rollbacks 362. Interpretation: on the held-out subset, the controller clearly improves over degraded direct segmentation and modestly but consistently improves over v2. The main limitation remains low absolute accept rate under extreme degradation (10.7%), mostly because 165/300 still fail before a reliable anchor can be obtained.
